title: Compress log files older than a number of days
summary: Finds the log files in a folder that have not changed for more than a set number of days and compresses each one with gzip. Each file becomes a smaller .gz file, which zcat or zless can still read. You see the list before anything changes.

aliases.text: compress log files older than N days
find and gzip old log files
free disk space by compressing logs
rotate old logs manually with gzip
сжать старые логи старше N дней

steps.explain: Preview: list the .log files whose last change is more than DAYS days ago. -mtime +30 means older than 30 full days. Nothing changes yet.
steps.expect: Paths such as logs/myapp/old.log. An empty output means no file is that old.

placeholders.name: DAYS
placeholders.description: Age in days; files older than this are compressed

steps.explain: Compress each old log. gzip writes a .gz file and removes the original; -v prints the name of each file it replaces.
steps.expect: One line per file, such as: ./old.log: ... -- replaced with ./old.log.gz
Paths ending in .log.gz for the files that were compressed.

rollback.explain: Unpack the compressed logs again. This restores every .log.gz file in the folder, so check the list first.

warnings: A program that is still writing to a log keeps writing to the old file after it is replaced, so those lines are lost. Do not compress logs that a running program uses; rotate them first with logrotate.
Compressing removes the original file. Test a copy first if the logs matter.
